key_insight: Pretrained text-to-video diffusion models (combined with large‑language model priors) can be adapted in a data‑efficient way to produce temporally coherent, stroke‑by‑stroke sketching processes rather than static images.
problem_solved: Most generative sketch models ignore the temporal, sequential nature of drawing and require large paired datasets; this work enables controllable, interpretable sketch generation that reproduces the natural ordering and refinement of strokes with minimal data.
method: Adapt pretrained text‑to‑video diffusion models to generate frame sequences that represent progressive sketch strokes, leveraging the video model’s temporal priors.
Incorporate large language model priors to guide stroke ordering and high‑level semantic structure for sketches.
Use a lightweight, data‑efficient fine‑tuning / adapter strategy so the system learns sketching dynamics from small sketch datasets while retaining rich video priors.
impact: Enables creation of interpretable, editable sketching processes for design, education, and human–AI co‑creation while reducing data and compute needs; makes sequential generation accessible to practitioners building sketch animation, interactive tools, or sketch-conditioned workflows.
visual_elements: Before vs After: static sketch image (left) vs stroke‑by‑stroke animation (right) to illustrate the sequential output
Model diagram: pretrained video diffusion + LLM priors -> lightweight adapters/fine‑tuning -> sequential sketch frames
Stroke timeline: sampled frames showing progressive refinement and stroke ordering over time
Bar chart or table: comparison of data required / quality metrics (few-shot adaptation vs from‑scratch training)
paper_title: VideoSketcher: Video Models Prior Enable Versatile Sequential Sketch Generation
paper_authors: Hui Ren, Yuval Alaluf, Omer Bar Tal, Alexander Schwing, Antonio Torralba
